The complainant is a first-year BSc Neuroscience Technology student at the college in Deralakatte. items.title: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall near Andhra coast, brings destructive winds and heavy rain
items.summary: Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab continued to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 morning, bringing destructive winds and torrential rain that uprooted trees, damaged electricity infrastructure and inundated low-lying areas. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the landfall process was expected to continue for several more hours. The storm began crossing the coast in the early hours of October 28, near the stretch between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam. The IMD reported sustained wind speeds of 125 to 135 kmph, with gusts reaching 150 kmph. Its northern spiral band had moved further inland, while the centre remained close to the coastline. North coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded extremely heavy rainfall overnight. Kannuripalem in Anakapalli district received around 263 mm of rain in the 24 hours ending at 8 am on October 28, according to the state Directorate of Economics and Statistics. Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district recorded a similar amount, while a police battalion campus in Visakhapatnam received around 260 mm. Thirty-nine automatic weather stations across Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram districts recorded more than 204.5 mm
